title: Linear and Symmetric Artificial Synapses Driven by Hydrogen Bonding for Accurate and Reliable Neuromorphic Computing
authors: Min Jong Lee, Sang Heon Lee, Dong Gyu Lee, Tae Hyuk Kim, Yubhin Cho, Gyeong Min Lee, Sung Su Yoon, Seon Joong Kim, Hyungju Ahn, Tae Kyung Lee*, and Jae Won Shim*
imageAlt: Editorial artwork emphasizing a hydrogen-bond network at a layered artificial-synapse interface; not experimental imagery
featuredQuestion: How can interfacial chemistry improve the linearity and stability of analog memory states?
featuredContribution: Hydrogen bonding at the polymer–perovskite interface suppresses traps and stabilizes analog switching, improving the linearity needed for neuromorphic computation.
featuredMetrics: >8× lower interfacial trap density · 50 analog states retained for >10⁴ s
